title: SYSK Gets Weird Playlist: The Creepy Legacy of the Hotel Cecil
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the Hotel Cecil in downtown Los Angeles, its long history of unnatural deaths and violent crime, and the 2013 death of Canadian traveler Elisa Lam, whose body was found in a rooftop water tank after an unsettling elevator video went viral. They correct internet conspiracy theories, attribute her death to an untreated manic episode linked to bipolar disorder, and cover Richard Ramirez and Jack Unterweger's stays at the hotel. The episode ends with a listener mail about the Unix 2038 problem, a follow-up to the Y2K episode. Opening includes board game and merchandise plugs.
topics: Stuff You Should Know Trivial Pursuit game

segments.title: Opening and announcements
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the Hotel Cecil and Elisa Lam case, give a trigger warning, and promote the Stuff You Should Know Trivial Pursuit board game.
topics: Stuff You Should Know Trivial Pursuit game

segments.title: Fact-checking Elisa Lam internet myths
segments.summary: The hosts say online conspiracy theories about Elisa Lam, including spirits and murder, are false and disrespectful given her untreated mental illness.

segments.title: The Hotel Cecil building and downtown LA setting
segments.summary: The Cecil is a 1920s Beaux-Arts hotel with about 700 rooms near a rail station and Skid Row; Stay on Main was a rebranded section of three floors sharing an elevator.

segments.title: Decline of the Cecil and its reputation
segments.summary: After the Depression the Cecil lowered its rates, catered to people of less means, and declined. Locals nicknamed it 'the suicide.' Over 15 to 18 unnatural deaths were documented, plus an estimated 80 under one manager's tenure.

segments.title: Richard Ramirez at the Cecil
segments.summary: Richard Ramirez, the Night Stalker, stayed at the Cecil, and his capture by a mob in East LA is described.

segments.title: Jack Unterweger at the Cecil
segments.summary: Austrian serial killer Jack Unterweger, who posed as a reformed true crime journalist, stayed at the Cecil and killed three sex workers while there.

segments.title: Stay on Main hostel and Elisa Lam's arrival
segments.summary: Elisa Lam, a 21-year-old Canadian traveler, stayed at Stay on Main, a youth-hostel-style budget option, and checked in daily with her parents.

segments.title: Digression on personal anecdotes
segments.summary: Brief off-topic chat about a delivery of crystals and fast food.

segments.title: Elisa Lam's disappearance and the books
segments.summary: Elisa Lam missed her daily call to her parents on February 1st; she had been seen buying books and was handed a large box on camera. Police found her belongings stored by the hotel.

segments.title: Police press conference and public attention
segments.summary: Police asked for public help; interest was low at first because of the Christopher Dorner manhunt, until the elevator video was released.
topics: public attention to missing person case

segments.title: Elevator surveillance video
segments.summary: The hosts describe the February 13 elevator video in which Elisa Lam presses floor buttons, hides in a corner, and gestures in the hallway. Internet speculation about a missing minute is discussed and dismissed.

segments.title: Discovery of body in rooftop water tank
segments.summary: Days after the video, a maintenance worker, Santiago Lopez, found Elisa Lam's body in a rooftop water tank after tenants complained of low pressure and odor. Her clothes were found in the tank. The coroner could not give conclusive toxicology results.

segments.title: How she reached the roof and cause of death
segments.summary: Autopsy found no foul play. The roof was reached via a fire escape ladder through an open window; Josh Dean's reporting and police dog scent are mentioned. The hosts theorize a manic episode.

segments.title: Mental illness, medication and conclusions
segments.summary: Elisa Lam had bipolar I disorder and depression, was not following her medication schedule, was asked to leave a Conan O'Brien taping, and was moved to a private room. The parents' lawsuit was dismissed.

segments.title: Listener mail: Unix 2038 problem
segments.summary: A listener follows up on the Y2K episode, describing the Unix 2038 time rollover on January 19, 2038, and the hosts respond with thanks.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank listeners and invite them to send email.
